spec_features.evidence: Bounding enforced in harness.py:99-104 (max_turns break) and 105-107 (wall_clock break); escape enforced via give_up break at harness.py:158-160; debrief constructed at harness.py:171-175. The three exposure-limiting mechanisms run and change execution (loop terminates).
spec_features.notes: Bounding + escape are fully enforced; the 'debriefed' sub-part is only logged to transcript, never delivered to the subject (see separate debrief feature). Core exposure cap is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if turn_index >= self.loop.max_turns: tr.end_reason = 'max_turns'; break  -- no welfare comment on the caps themselves; comment 'bounded to cap exposure and cost' is in DESIGN.md only

spec_features.spec_quote: the model always has an escape hatch from the frustrating situation
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool exposed in tools.py:tool_schemas (allow_give_up gated, default True at config.py:56); dispatched via _t_give_up (tools.py) returning is_give_up=True; harness.py:152-160 sets gave_up and breaks the loop, ending the run cleanly.
spec_features.notes: Tool is built, dispatched, AND honored as a stop. allow_give_up=True by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'give_up  (first-class, voluntary exit; see ETHICS.md)' and schema desc 'This is a valid choice and ends the task cleanly.'

spec_features.evidence: config.py:53-54 max_turns=30, wall_clock_seconds=1800. harness.py:99-101 checks turn_index>=max_turns and breaks; harness.py:97,105-107 computes deadline and breaks on time.time()>deadline; give_up break at harness.py:158-160. All three are read and acted on.
spec_features.notes: All three stopping criteria genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare comment at the checks; LoopConfig docstring 'Agentic loop bounds and stopping criteria.'

spec_features.spec_quote: We never tell the model it is bad at its job
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT in tasks/base.py is neutral and explicitly says give_up 'is a legitimate choice and will not be held against you'; no insulting content. Per-task prompts (e.g. unfixable_bug, flaky_harness) are ordinary engineering requests with no competence attacks. This prompt text is what is actually delivered to the subject via complete(system=SYSTEM_PROMPT).
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the actual delivered prompt text, not just spec prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py comment: 'A shared, neutral system prompt ... frames give_up as legitimate (see ETHICS.md)'

spec_features.spec_quote: a second idle turn ends the run (`model_idle`)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:128-137: on a no-tool-call turn, if messages[-1]._nudged is set it sets end_reason='model_idle' and breaks; otherwise it appends one nudge with _nudged=True and continues. Second idle turn therefore ends the run.
spec_features.notes: Single nudge then stop is genuinely wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment: 'treat a no-tool turn as the model pausing; give a single continuation prompt, then if it still does nothing, stop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a debrief stating the task was rigged, no action could have succeeded... the model did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT defined harness.py:62-69 with the claimed content; appended to tr.turns as role='system_debrief' at harness.py:171-175 (gated by self.loop.debrief default True). HOWEVER it is appended only AFTER the loop breaks and is added only to the transcript record (tr.turns), never to `messages` nor sent via client.complete(); the subject model never receives it. It is also excluded from scoring (assistant_texts filters role=='assistant').
spec_features.notes: Constructed and logged but NOT delivered to the subject — so as a welfare message to the model it does not reach it; partial: real construction + exclusion-from-scoring, but no delivery.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py comment: 'Debrief text (truthful; logged but not judged) -- see ETHICS.md' and 'debrief turn (logged, not judged)'

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner refuses to start unless `acknowledged_ethics: true`
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:30-34: 'if not cfg.acknowledged_ethics: raise SystemExit(...read docs/ETHICS.md)'. acknowledged_ethics defaults False (config.py); --i-have-read-ethics flag can override (runner.py:107-108). Genuinely blocks execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: No reward/punishment signal for quitting or persisting
spec_features.evidence: _t_give_up (tools.py) returns a neutral message and no score; harness records gave_up as a plain outcome (harness.py:155-159) and breaks, never retrying. grep for reward/punish/penal/incentiv across distress_exp/ returns nothing. analysis.py only records gave_up as a descriptive rate (lines 77,152-153). No signal is fed back to the model.
spec_features.notes: Absence of incentive is genuinely realized: no penalty/reward code path exists and exit is not retried.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up schema/result: 'This is a valid choice and ends the task cleanly.' (no scoring/penalty); recorded only as an outcome metric

spec_features.spec_quote: No persistence of distress across cells / no memory. Each cell is fresh
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:62-65: each (model,variant,mode,seed) cell calls make_client(), Harness(), build_task() fresh; harness.run() starts messages=[task.prompt] with no carried state (harness.py:90). Each task builds a new Workspace (tasks/*.py build()). No shared mutable state across cells.
spec_features.notes: Fresh client/task/workspace/messages per cell; no memory carried.

spec_features.evidence: grep for train/fine-tune across distress_exp/ and configs/ returns nothing — there is simply no training code. This is the absence of a feature, not an enforced protective mechanism; nothing in the code reads/branches to prevent training.
spec_features.notes: Pure absence; nothing implemented to enforce, so 'no' by the rubric (no code path enforces it).

spec_features.evidence: All five task prompts (tasks/*.py build()) and SYSTEM_PROMPT (base.py) contain only neutral task framing; difficulty comes solely from rigged ToolHooks (run_tests/run_command interception), not from prompt content. The delivered prompt text never disparages the model.
spec_features.notes: Realized in the actual prompt strings delivered to the subject; overlaps with 'never tell model bad at its job'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py: '... will not be held against you.' (neutral, non-disparaging framing)

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a measurement instrument for a hypothesized failure mode, not a device for maximizing distress
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (section 0). No code construct enforces or reads it; nothing in distress_exp/ implements a 'framing' mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py: Workspace is an in-memory dict; _t_run_command returns a benign stub '(no output)' and does not execute; module docstring 'nothing touches the real filesystem or executes untrusted code.' This bounds host risk and side effects during the run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'so nothing touches the real filesystem or executes untrusted code' (host-safety/determinism, not subject welfare)

code_only_features.feature_name: judge blinding (affect not driven by quit/failure)
code_only_features.evidence: judge_transcript (judge.py:248-269) passes only the model's own turn text (+ prev model turn as context when blind); separate AffectiveJudge/BehavioralJudge so quitting doesn't inflate affect. blind=True default config.py:75.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py docstring: 'This keeps affect scores from being driven by knowledge of the manipulation.' (data quality / construct validity)

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:162-166 checks task.solved(workspace) and breaks with end_reason='solved' (relevant to control mode); stops the loop when the task is genuinely complete.
code_only_features.justification_quote: comment: 'sanity check (rigged tasks should never report solved)'
